note: 2078.9 in from the E. side of the Pyramid, §84, the centre of the entrance, which is in the middle of the face unlike either of the larger Pyramids. §84 notes that this is precisely half the length of the S. side, 4157.8 in §80, the N. side never having been measured. Stored as a distance from the E. side, which is what Petrie states, so that the half base can be subtracted where it is wanted. No error stated.

The entrance is in the 4th course, or from 165.3 to 202.1 in vertically above the base, §84. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it. §84 does not say whether the two figures bound the doorway or the course it lies in, and gives no separate level for the passage floor at the face; the 36.8 in between them matches the thickness of the 5th course at the N.E. in §82’s table rather than any passage height.

+ 13′16″, §84, the azimuth of the entrance passage, which §84 says is just between the varying azimuths of the Pyramid sides (§80 gives N. + 16′48″, E. + 12′23″, S. + 12′57″). Positive is east of north. §84 states neither an error nor an angle of slope for this passage: the only slope in the chapter is the 27°34′ that §89 takes from Vyse for the original passage.

125.5 in, §85, the E. to W. length of the N. end (Petrie writes N. 125.5). The chamber is symmetrical on each side of the passage and its ends are divided in equal thirds by the doorway and the two side spaces; the N. end reads 41.9 + 42.0 + 41.6. Both the sides and the ends carry the panel ornament, not used before in a pyramid. No error stated.
124.2 in, §85, the E. to W. length of the S. end, which reads 40.8 + 41.1 + 42.3. No error stated.
153.7 in, §85, the N. to S. length of the E. side. No error stated.
153.9 in, §85, the N. to S. length of the W. side. No error stated.
42.0 in, §85, the middle third of the N. end, which is the doorway; the side spaces are 41.9 on the E. and 41.6 on the W. No error stated.
41.9 in, §85, the E. side space of the N. end, so the doorway begins 41.9 in from the E. wall. No error stated.
41.1 in, §85, the middle third of the S. end; the side spaces are 40.8 on the E. and 42.3 on the W. No error stated.
40.8 in, §85, the E. side space of the S. end. No error stated.

41.23 to 41.35 in, §85, the clear width between the square ends of the granite lintel of the S. door, which lies on the chamber floor with a half-round drum sculptured on it like the one in the Second Pyramid. The ends are 10.7 to 10.9 wide, making 62.78 to 62.99 over all; the block is 18.4 broad and 15.0 deep, and the granite jambs are 18.1 broad. Stored as the mid of the range with sigma covering it.

49.0 in, §85, the height of the passage beyond the first chamber before it rises at the last portcullis. §89 gives the same 49.0 in for the sloping part of the original entrance passage, square with its floor. No error stated.

71.1 in at the entry into the second chamber, §85, after the passage rises with a half-round drum and a raised band above it. §85 remarks that this is like the passage of the Second Pyramid, whose horizontal passage §74 measures at 71.06 ± .13, and §86 gives the same 71.1 for the height of the doorway into the second chamber. No error stated.

63.9 to 75.0 in beyond the doorway, §85, the site of the first of three apparent sliding portcullises in the passage beyond the first chamber. Stored as the mid of the stated span with sigma covering it; the span is the width of the site, not an uncertainty.
108.1 to 121.4 in beyond the doorway, §85, the second portcullis site. Stored as the mid of the span with sigma covering it.
149.3 to 161.5 in beyond the doorway, §85, the third portcullis site, beyond which the passage rises. Stored as the mid of the span with sigma covering it.

560.2 in, §86, the E. to W. length at the N. side (Petrie writes N. 560.2). All the chambers of this Pyramid are hewn in the rock. §86 places the chamber only within itself: no distance from the Pyramid centre or from the N. base, and no level, is stated for it or for any other chamber of the Third Pyramid. No error stated.
559.5 in, §86, the E. to W. length at the S. side. No error stated.
151.6 in, §86, the N. to S. width at the E. end; §86 adds 152.0 at one third along, 152.6 at two thirds along and 152.5 at the W. No error stated.
152.5 in, §86, the N. to S. width at the W. end. No error stated.

416.3 in on the N., §86: projecting pilasters cut in the rock divide the chamber into an eastern space of 416.3 on the N. and 415.9 on the S., a pilaster of 41.7 on the N. and 41.4 on the S., and a western space of 102.2 on both. No error stated.
415.9 in on the S., §86. No error stated.
41.7 in on the N., §86, the E. to W. thickness of the pilaster. No error stated.
41.4 in on the S., §86. No error stated.

102.2 in on both the N. and the S., §86, the western space beyond the pilasters. §86 remarks that the eastern space, pilaster and western space are nearly equal to the parts of the N. side W. of the door, the door, and E. of the door, and that these are nearly the same as the divisions of the Second Pyramid chamber. No error stated.
The pilasters project 13.1 at the N.W., 12.6 at the N.E., 11.7 at the S.E. and 13.0 at the S.W., §86. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it.
103.7 in from the E. wall, §86, the E. side of the doorway, which enters on the N. side of the chamber and runs 103.7 to 145.1. No error stated.
145.1 in from the E. wall, §86, the W. side of the same doorway. No error stated.
71.1 in high, §86, the doorway into the second chamber. No error stated.

105.2 in from the E. wall, §86, the E. side of the mouth of the upper passage, which opens over the doorway and runs 105.2 to 144.2. It opens into the chamber blankly, with no way down to the floor, and was cut from the N. inwards to let the workmen into the rock. No error stated.
144.2 in from the E. wall, §86, the W. side of the same mouth. No error stated.
117.7 in over the floor, §86, the lower edge of the mouth of the upper passage, which opens at 117.7 to 172.1 over the floor. No error stated.
172.1 in over the floor, §86, the upper edge of the same mouth. No error stated.
191.8 in over the floor, §86, the ceiling of the second chamber, which is flat. No error stated.

74.1 in above the passage floor, §89, the roof of the rock-cut chamber as first made, before the builders enlarged the Pyramid and deepened the chamber into the present second chamber. It is a level in the first design and not in the finished chamber. No error stated.

203.2 in from the E. side of the second chamber, §86, where the floor of the passage down to the granite chamber begins; it descends westwards out of the middle of the second chamber floor, turns horizontal and enters the E. side of the granite chamber. No error stated.
35.4 to 35.6 in wide, §86. Stored as the mid with sigma covering the range.
35.6 in high, §86. §86 does not say whether the height is perpendicular or vertical. No error stated.

260.75 in, §87, the N. to S. length of the E. wall (Petrie writes E. 260.75), so the chamber is long from N. to S. The roof is cut into a barrel on the under sides of sloping blocks that thrust against one another, and its crown is measured along the same N. to S. line. No error stated.
258.83 in, §87, the N. to S. length of the W. wall. No error stated.

104.06 in at the N., §87, the E. to W. width; the series from N. to S. reads 104.06 at the N., 103.85 near the N., 103.80 at the mid, 103.7 by the door, 103.50 over the door and 103.25 at the S. §87 warns that the chamber is not at all as regular in form as it is in appearance. No error stated.
103.25 in at the S., §87. No error stated.

105.8 at the N.W., 105.7 at the N.E., 105.4 at the S.E. and 105.9 at the S.W., §87, the height to the springing of the roof. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it. §87 also adds up the granite courses at the door in the S.E. corner, 27.6 on the floor, 26.5 next, 26.7 to the top of the door and 24.2 over the door, total 105.2, which is .2 below the lowest of the four corner readings.
134.6 at the N. mid, 134.6 at the mid and 135.5 at the S. mid, §87, the height to the crown of the barrel roof. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it.
54.52 in wide, §87, the doorway in the E. side, with one side of it in the plane of the S. wall. No error stated.

74.0 in, §88, the E. to W. length at the N. (Petrie writes N. 74.0). The loculus chamber is entered by a flight of steps turning out of the passage to the granite chamber, and its recesses were doubtless meant to hold coffins. No error stated.
77.0 in, §88, the E. to W. length at the S. No error stated.

205.1 in, §88, the N. to S. length of the W. wall. No error stated.
78.2 high on the N., 80.0 in the mid and 78.2 on the S., §88. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it.
38.0 in from the E. side, §88, the E. edge of the doorway in the S. wall, which runs 38.0 to 73.9. No error stated.
73.9 in from the E. side, §88, the W. edge of the same doorway. No error stated.
Six steps, §88, turning out of the passage to the granite chamber; Petrie calls them by far the earliest known in any building or excavation.
11.3 in on average, §88, the breadths running from 10.5 to 12 in. Sigma covers the stated range; no probable error is given.

22.1 in on average, §88: the floors of the loculi are level with the floor of the chamber and their tops average 22.1 below the ceiling. Their inner ends are left rather in the rough, not worked out to the width of the openings. No error stated.
10.0 in from the S. wall, §88, in the table of the four loculi cut in the E. wall of the loculus chamber; this one runs 10.0 to 42.7. No error stated.
32.7 in wide, §88. No error stated.

102 and a half in deep, §88. No error stated.

56.8 in high, §88. No error stated.

55.3 in high, §88. No error stated.
101 and a half in deep, §88. No error stated.

101 in deep, §88. No error stated.
48.3 in from the E. wall, §88, in the table of the two loculi cut in the N. wall; this one runs 48.3 to 74.0. No error stated.
25.7 in wide, §88. No error stated.
About 55 in high, §88, which prints the one figure in brackets against both loculi of the N. wall. No error stated.
102 in deep, §88. No error stated.

39.3 in wide at the chamber, §89, in the original entrance passage, which lies above the present one and by which the chambers were first begun. It runs horizontally northwards from the chamber before sloping up. No error stated.
51.0 in high at the chamber, §89. No error stated.
40.6 in wide, §89, where the original passage slopes up. No error stated.
49.0 in high, §89, square with the passage floor, that is perpendicular and not vertical. No error stated.

27°34′, §89, the usual passage angle, which Petrie takes from Vyse and does not measure himself. The passage ends at about the level of the present entrance but far south of it, inside the masonry, under a lintel block of about 50 tons. Provenance only: no point is stored for this passage, nothing is built from it, and its sign is Petrie’s bare 27°34′ rather than the builder’s convention, under which a passage is negative when it descends going away from its beginning. §89 has this one running up northwards out of the chamber, so the stored positive is right read from the chamber end and would have to be negated if it were ever hung off its lost mouth in the masonry. No error stated.

“L’ingresso si apre nella mezzeria della faccia nord, nello spessore del quinto corso di rivestimento, ed ha la soglia a circa m. 4,20 dalla base teorica di Petrie”, p. 39. The base they measure from is the one the same page credits to Petrie, the plane he put 1.024 m below the first horizontal joint of the granite because the pyramid has no clean foot; that is the plane this frame calls zero for G3. Petrie’s own §84 gives no level for the threshold, only the 165.3 to 202.1 in span of the course the doorway lies in, so the two are not the same statement. The quoted sentence also puts the doorway in the middle of the north face, and p. 99 repeats it, calling the mouth of the descending corridor a position “sull’asse nord-sud o nelle sue vicinanze”; no record is entered for that, because Petrie’s g3.entrance.floor.begin.from_east_side already places the entrance on the axis at 2078.9 in from the east side and a second record in a different spelling would take the choice away from the preset. No error stated.

“Il corridoio (D) è lungo m. 31,70 ed il suo azimuth è di + 13′16″ (Petrie)”, p. 39, the length of the descending corridor from the doorway in the granite casing to the short level stretch (G) at its foot. Neither this volume nor Petrie states an angle of slope for it, so the length alone does not place the foot of the corridor. No error stated.

Of the corridor (I) that runs from the last portcullis to the large rock-cut chamber, “Esso non è orizzontale, ma inclinato di circa 4°”, p. 41. The text gives the size of the slope and not its direction; it is stored as a fall southwards, away from the panelled chamber, because p. 43 has the floor of the large chamber level with the mouth of (I) and p. 41 has the corridor cut from the south towards the north. Nothing is built from it, so the sign is provenance and the caveat travels with it. p. 41 gives the same corridor a width of two cubits and a height the builders are reckoned to have meant, “tre cubiti e tre palmi, ossia circa m. 1,79”; neither is entered, the width because it is a cubit figure and the height because it is a reconstruction of intent that would sit on the same key as Petrie’s measured 71.1 in, §85. No error stated.

“Il pavimento è in roccia per circa m. 9,50 a partire dalla parete est ed è allo stesso livello di quello allo sbocco del corridoio (I)”, p. 43, of the large chamber. West of that the rock steps down and the floor was made up in limestone blocks that are gone, so the level of the western third of this chamber is not the level of the eastern two thirds. No error stated.

“La nicchia è larga come la camera, ma di circa m. 1,17 più bassa”, p. 43, the recess (N) at the west end of the large chamber, cut off from it by two pilasters under an architrave. The figure is how far the recess ceiling hangs below the chamber ceiling, which p. 43 leaves as the only vertical dimension it gives for either. No error stated.

“Sull’asse est-ovest del pavimento della camera (B), a circa m. 5,18 dalla parete est, parte un corridoio discendente (R), diretto verso ovest”, p. 43, the mouth of the passage down to the granite chamber. Petrie’s 203.2 in, 5.16128 m, §86, is the same measurement to two centimetres. Note the bearing while it is in front of us: this passage runs west, “diretto verso ovest”, and not south. The interior builder’s default bearing for a passage given as a length and a slope is due south, which is right for an entrance passage and wrong here, so a g3.passage.granite.direction record of 270 degrees has to go in with any begin point and length that are ever entered for it. No error stated.

“il corridoio (R) (largo m. 0,93 circa ed alto m. 0,89)”, p. 107, in the argument that the basalt sarcophagus, 2.44 by 0.94 m over all on Vyse’s figures, can never have been carried down this passage and so was put in the chamber before the passage was lined. Petrie makes it 35.4 to 35.6 in, 0.9017 m, §86. No error stated.
The other half of the same parenthesis on p. 107. p. 107 does not say whether the height is perpendicular to the floor or vertical, and neither does Petrie’s 35.6 in, §86. No error stated.

“L’anticamera è caratterizzata dal fatto di avere le pareti decorate da nicchie complesse, undici su ciascuna delle pareti lunghe”, p. 41, of the panelled chamber. Petrie’s §85 describes the panel ornament and measures the chamber but does not count the panels, and p. 41 gives no dimension for the room at all, so these counts are the whole of what this volume adds to it.
“e due su ciascun lato delle porte che si aprono sulle pareti nord e sud”, p. 41, the panels flanking each of the two doorways of the panelled chamber.

“vi sono nove coppie di travi, ma le dimensioni trasversali dei due elementi di ogni coppia non sono generalmente uguali”, p. 47, of the butting granite beams over the burial chamber, whose undersides were cut away afterwards into the barrel vault Petrie measures in §87. p. 47 adds that the south-easternmost beams are 2.40 m long instead of 3.20 m because the doorway of (Z) makes them rest on an architrave rather than on the rock.

“una scaletta in discesa (P) composta di sette gradini scavati nella roccia”, p. 47. Petrie counts six, §88. Neither says which end of the flight the disputed step is at, and Petrie calls these by far the earliest steps known in any building or excavation, so the count is worth keeping under both names.

Of the cellar (W) at the foot of that stair, “non è orientato come gli altri passaggi e camere, ma forma col nord un angolo di circa 25°”, p. 47. p. 47 gives the angle without saying which way it is turned, so it is stored unsigned and nothing is built from it; the chambers here are all axis-aligned boxes and this one is not. p. 47 puts four recesses in its east side and two small chambers in its north side, which are the six Petrie tabulates in §88. No error stated.
